title: service-resilience-collab-field-notes-42-day-experiment
content:
Overview:

Working notes for a 42-day cross-functional experiment to reduce P99 tail latency spikes and validate a service-level objective (SLO) decomposition pattern across product, serving-runtime, infra, and SRE. This is a field-oriented companion doc (not the canonical playbook) — experimental tactics, raw observations, and triage heuristics that we can convert into formal runbooks after the pilot.

Background / Motivation:
- Recent customer incidents show recurring P99 spikes on model-serving routes during peak bursts and backend degradation (cache misses, DB timeouts).
- We need a pragmatic way to: (1) define layered SLOs (edge vs. model vs. storage), (2) make cross-team runbooks actionable, and (3) validate automation that routes traffic to fallbacks without customer-visible error-rate increases.
- Goal is to prove a 3-layer SLO decomposition (API latency SLO, model-queueing SLO, datastore-throughput SLO) and a collision-avoidant rollout process across Dedicated and Hosted deployments.

Primary objectives (success criteria):
- Reduce P99 tail latency spikes by >= 25% for prioritized routes during the 42-day pilot window compared to the previous 42 days (measured by synthetic probes + real traffic percentiles).
- Demonstrate safe automated fallback for the model layer with no increase in 5xx error-rate > 0.05% during canary.
- Produce a validated, handoff-ready cross-team runbook + SLO ownership map that product teams can adopt.

Scope (what we're experimenting on):
- Targeted surface: /v1/generate and /v1/chat (top 10 tenant routes by token-volume) on the hosted API and one Dedicated pool (eu-west-1-dedicated).
- Timebox: 42 days split into 3 x 14-day sprints.
- Exclusions: Embeddings pipeline, offline batch jobs, and on-prem private deployments (these may be onboarded later).

Stakeholders & RACI (draft):
- Product (hosted-api): Responsible for route prioritization and customer impact evaluation. (R: Maya Liu)
- Serving Runtime: Responsible for model fallback logic, batching, and KV cache improvements. (R: Ethan Patel)
- Infra / Platform: Responsible for autoscaling config, reserved capacity for Dedicated, and capacity simulations. (R: Andre Gomes)
- SRE / Observability: Responsible for signal definition, alerting, and runbook activation. (R: Sofia Martinez)
- Security & Compliance: Consult for any cross-tenant fallback behavior that may affect customer isolation. (C: Priya Kapoor)

42-day sprint plan (high-level):
- Sprint 0 (days 0-14): "Signal & Baseline"
  - Define and instrument metrics: request_latency_ms.{p50,p95,p99}, model_queue_time_ms, kv_cache_hit_ratio, db_95th_ms.
  - Synthetic probes: hourly per-tenant latency probes that mimic top-10 production prompt lengths.
  - Baseline capture: collect 42-day historical percentiles for comparison.
  - Small experiments: enable prefix KV caching for two low-risk routes.
- Sprint 1 (days 15-28): "Mitigation and Safe Rollouts"
  - Implement model-level fallback variant with conservative quality threshold (e.g., beam/temperature change or smaller model).
  - Canary rollout to 5% traffic on Hosted and to a single Dedicated shard.
  - Tune autoscaling and batching knobs in infra playground; stress test with replayed traces.
- Sprint 2 (days 29-42): "Automation & Handoff"
  - Add automated routing policy: if model_queue_time_ms > X and kv_cache_hit_ratio < Y -> route to fallback variant.
  - Validate that automated action reduces P99 spikes during synthetic storm tests.
  - Draft cross-team runbook, SLO ownersheet, and postmortem template.

SLO definitions (candidate):
- Customer-facing API latency SLO: 99th percentile request latency < 800ms across top-10 routes (measured across rolling 30d windows).
- Model serving SLO: 99th percentile model-queue+inference latency < 600ms per model-variant.
- Storage dependency SLO: datastore 95th percentile write latency < 40ms and read latencies < 30ms for KV cache.
Notes: these thresholds are intentionally aggressive for the experiment. We'll tune after Sprint 0 baselines.

Instrumentation & observability checklist (must-pass before canary):
- Tracing: end-to-end trace IDs propagated from edge to model container and datastore.
- Telemetry: request-level tags include route_id, tenant_id, sequence_length_bucket, model_variant.
- Alerts: temporary experiment alerts: SLO-breach-warning (p99>threshold for 10m), fallback-invocations-rate, cache_hit_drop.
- Dashboards: SLO heatmap by tenant, model-variant latency waterfall, autoscaler headroom.

Runbook skeleton (for SRE/oncall):
- Trigger: SLO-breach-warning -> runbook steps:
  1) Identify correlated signal: is model_queue_time the dominant contributor? (trace waterfall)
  2) If yes, trigger manual fallback for the affected route(s) via console (instructions + CLI snippet).
  3) If fallback fails or increases 5xx, rollback fallback and escalate to serving-runtime oncall.
  4) Post-incident: capture top 3 suspect root causes and assign action items.

Traffic routing rules (experimental):
- Conservative default: only route to fallback for requests with seq_len_bucket <= defined threshold, avoid routing long-context requests.
- Graceful degrade: reduce max_tokens for fallback variant if model latency remains high.

Risk matrix (draft):
- Risk: Fallback reduces output quality -> mitigations: restrict to low-risk tenants and add human-readable notice for beta tenants; measure quality via sampling.
- Risk: Autoscaler thrash during synthetic storms -> mitigations: set cooldowns, enable surge buffer on Dedicated pool.
- Risk: Alert fatigue -> mitigations: temporary experiment-only alerts, de-dupe via aggregated targets.

Quality checks / evaluation plan:
- Daily sampling of responses from fallback vs primary model for semantic drift (blind A/B evals by product).
- Regression threshold: if fallback leads to >8% drop in baseline score for top-3 prompt families, pause rollout.

Meeting cadence & rituals:
- Daily 15m standup (experiment channel) during canary period (Sprint 1+2).
- Twice-weekly tactical sync (30m) with product, runtime, infra (agenda: blockers, metrics, next steps).
- End-of-sprint review + artifacts (14-day demos + decision log).

Open questions / unknowns:
- What is a safe quality threshold to prefer fallback? (Product to propose sample-based threshold by day 10)
- Can we automatically decide tenant eligibility for fallback based on historical quality sensitivity? (Future work)
- Any legal/compliance edge cases with cross-tenant fallbacks? (Security/Legal to review)

Action items (first 7 days):
- A: Instrument model_queue_time_ms + tagging (Ethan)
- B: Create synthetic probe harness for top-10 routes (SRE / Sofia)
- C: Product to finalize tenant list and quality thresholds (Maya)
- D: Infra to reserve a small Dedicated shard and configure surge buffer (Andre)
- E: Runbook draft + alert rules committed to repo (Sofia + Andre)

Notes to self (working):
- Keep the experiment limited in blast radius — prefer conservative heuristics that are reversible.
- Emphasize measurable outcomes: latency percentiles + quality sampling.
- Record every manual intervention as a Jira ticket tagged RED-EXPERIMENT so we can analyze human-in-the-loop costs.

Next steps:
- Confirm instrumentation targets and open the RED-4132 epic with subtasks before day 3.
- Schedule the experiment kickoff demo with VP eng and product at day 5.

End of field notes. Will iterate into a formal runbook after end-of-pilot review.

Raw decision log (appendix):
- 2026-03-12: Decided 42-day length to allow two full 14-day sprint cycles and a buffer for slow rollouts.
- 2026-03-15: Chosen initial SLO thresholds are intentionally tight; will relax after Sprint 0.
